name: Hero's Journey (audience as hero)
summary: Cast the audience or customer as the hero who leaves the known world, meets a guide, faces trials and returns transformed.
references: Joseph Campbell, The Hero with a Thousand Faces (1949)
title_style: Narrative phrase titles, under 10 words, naming the stage of the journey.

sequence.purpose: Introduce the hero in their ordinary world.
The ordinary world and its limits.
The guide and the tool they offer.
The elixir the audience can take home.

pitfalls: Making the company or speaker the hero instead of the audience.
Using every stage of the full journey; most talks need only a few.
Trials with no real risk, so the turning point feels flat.

example.topic: A fictional bookkeeping app told through one shop owner's journey
outline: Meet Jun, a shop owner who does her own books
An advisor hands her a simple ledger app
The first month of receipts is a mess
Audit day: every number checks out
Your guide is not the hero; you are
